headline: From dotfile scripts to an AI-tended, gamified IT learning quest site
summary: it-journey began in 2020 as a handful of Homebrew and machine-setup scripts plus a bashcrawl teaching game. In September 2021 it became a Jekyll site on the author's zer0 mistakes theme. Over the next four years it went through repeated rebuilds: collections were invented and then deleted, the theme was rewritten in place and later moved to a remote theme, and content arrived in bursts between long quiet gaps. From mid-2025 the repository changed character. AI workflows, validators and link checkers arrived, and 'quests' grew into a structured, tiered curriculum. By 2026 it had become a high-volume, agent-assisted publishing system with walkthrough-verification loops, shared runner kits and epic quest chains, with bots and AI-assisted commits making up a large share of the activity.

eras.title: Setup Scripts and Bashcrawl
eras.summary: The repository started as a toolbox of macOS Homebrew installers, GCP startup scripts and environment guides, first in init_apps and then in init_world. Level folders (lvl_0000, lvl_0001) brought in a bashcrawl game, an early sign of the leveled-learning idea. A brief mkdocs site was also tried.
eras.frontend: Apart from a short-lived mkdocs index page, there was no real site; visitors saw a README and setup guides.
eras.backend: Bash and PowerShell install scripts were moved between init_apps and init_world, and Windows setup scripts and a PowerShell profile were added.
transitions: from personal install scripts at the root to an organized init_world folder of per-platform guides
from loose scripts to a leveled bashcrawl learning concept

learnings.lesson: Gitignore IDE state from the first commit; Visual Studio .vs files were committed and later had to be removed.
Settle on one remote and branch flow early; this era is full of merges of 'remote master' that only shuffled small guide edits.

eras.title: Jekyll Site on zer0 Mistakes
eras.summary: In September 2021 the project became a Jekyll site on the zer0 mistakes theme, after tens of thousands of lines of churn. Content collections multiplied: quests, notes, cheats, quickstart, about and hobbies. The site also gained code-copy, a sitemap, Algolia search and CodeQL scanning.
eras.frontend: Visitors got a themed blog-like site with a sidebar, quickstart guides, notes, copy-to-clipboard code blocks, a sitemap and Algolia search.
eras.backend: Sass partials and includes were vendored and reorganized repeatedly, the old init_world and lvl folders were removed, and CodeQL and Google Tag Manager were added.
transitions: from a script repository to a Jekyll content site
from flat folders to many Jekyll collections (_notes, _quickstart, _hobbies, _quest)

learnings.lesson: Pick a theme strategy (vendored or remote) before customizing; vendoring here caused 30k-line deletions and repeated Sass reshuffles.
Design the collection taxonomy before creating many folders; _cheats was added and removed within a month, and posts were moved more than once.

eras.title: Polish, Domain, and Dark Mode
eras.summary: Activity slowed into intermittent fixes and features. Header, search bar and branding were fixed, the custom domain was set and then removed again, and dark mode and a particle.js background arrived. A Dockerfile and build script appeared at the end of the era.
eras.frontend: Visitors saw a rebranded header, dark mode, Jekyll documentation pages and an animated particle background.
eras.backend: Work went through PR-based merges, Gemfile.lock was removed, Algolia build errors were fixed, and Docker build tooling was cleaned up.
transitions: from rapid structural churn to incremental UI polish
from direct pushes to pull-request merges

learnings.lesson: Keep the lockfile. Deleting Gemfile.lock was followed by Gemfile compatibility and Algolia build fixes.
Decide on the domain before committing CNAME; it was created and deleted in the same month.

eras.title: Major Cleanup and Beta Rebuild
eras.summary: A 'Major Clean up' removed about 21k lines. In March 2023 the many collections were folded into a single pages directory under beta 0.2 and 0.3 releases. A quests section with a world map and glossary appeared in late 2023, followed by notes, SEO posts, a Docker setup and a UI overhaul with per-section navigation files.
eras.frontend: The site was relaunched as a beta with Penrose logos, a new search bar, breadcrumbs, back-to-top and dark color mode, followed by a quests world map, SEO articles and an auto-hiding navbar.
eras.backend: Collections were consolidated into pages/, a devcontainer and Dockerfile were added, navigation was split into per-section data files, and Front Matter CMS sync was introduced.
transitions: from many top-level collections to a consolidated pages/ tree
from a blog of notes to a quests-centered learning map

learnings.lesson: Fix the back-to-top feature once with a test; it was repaired in both 2023-11 and 2024-03.
Keep unrelated projects out of the site repo; bookstore inventory scripts and CSVs were added here and later had to be merged into worktrees.

eras.title: Remote Theme and Quiet Trickle
eras.summary: May 2024 brought a 71-commit cleanup burst. In June 2024 about 8,363 lines of local styling were deleted in favor of a remote theme, and Jupyter notebooks, zer0 shell tooling and Giscus comments were added. Then activity dropped to roughly one content commit a month for a year.
eras.frontend: Visitors saw Giscus comments, notebook-derived pages, and occasional new articles on Django, Excel, AI automation and ERP.
eras.backend: Layouts, includes and Sass were removed in favor of remote_theme, submodules were added, markdown-to-shell converters were built, and CodeQL was retargeted to main.
transitions: from a vendored theme to a remote zer0-mistakes theme
from active development to sporadic content drops

learnings.lesson: Moving to remote_theme earlier would have avoided years of in-repo Sass and layout fixes that this one commit discarded.
Use descriptive commit subjects; content additions shipped under subjects like 'test'.

eras.title: Automation and Quest Scaling
eras.summary: From July 2025 bots and AI-assisted commits appeared. AI content review, frontmatter validation, link checking and post organization became workflows. Quests became structured, with frontmatter, a validator, 72 generated placeholders and 32 Master Tier quests, and an Azure Static Web Apps deployment and an SEO project followed.
eras.frontend: Visitors saw gamified quests grouped by tier in filterable cards, SEO-tuned titles, and a regenerated quest home table.
eras.backend: Scripts were reorganized into core and development folders, and the repository gained an AI Evolution Engine, Link Health Guardian, a quest validator, a preview-generator plugin, a date-prefix renamer and a migration to the zer0-mistakes v0.17 navigation schema.
transitions: from hand-maintained pages to workflow-driven content validation
from ad-hoc quests to a tiered, schema-backed quest catalog

learnings.lesson: Don't commit generated reports; link-check result dumps and logs were added and removed again.
Enforce the frontmatter schema at creation time; bulk placeholder generation led to 318 validation errors that needed an automated fixer.

eras.title: Quest Framework Hardening and Pruning
eras.summary: Automation commits grew to dominate. A quest solutions framework, a v2 validator, link checker v3.0 with lychee, and a vendor-agnostic AI client were added. The site was then cut back: the posts and notebooks collections and 220 vendored wargame pages moved to other repos.
eras.frontend: Visitors gained contributor RPG character sheets, a split quickstart hub, a Bashcrawl learning path, level-prefixed quest URLs with redirects, and rebuilt top navigation with no 404s.
eras.backend: The repository gained a shared validator and scoring CLI, a single-source quest schema, a frontmatter normalization pass over 641 files, condensed agent prompts, and .claude/.cms/.quests directories.
transitions: from accumulating content to pruning it and moving it to sibling repos
from per-script link tools to one consolidated link-checker

learnings.lesson: Avoid vendoring third-party docs; the 220 OverTheWire pages added in April were extracted to a standalone repo two months later.
Pick one token name across workflows; tokens were renamed from GITHUB_TOKEN to PAT_TOKEN to GITHUB_PAT, and seven CI workflows later needed fixes.
Add a Liquid lint to CI; nested raw blocks broke the production Pages build.

eras.title: Agentic Fleet and Epic Quests
eras.summary: This was the busiest era, at 100 to 150 commits a month and mostly automation. Quest walkthroughs are now verified by agent loops and recorded to video. Workflows adopted the shared fleet runner kit and the claude-run action, and an MCP server exposes quests to agents. New content arrives as multi-chapter epics on home servers, PXE boot and legacy COBOL, and an Astro spike tests a possible move off Jekyll.
eras.frontend: Visitors see epic quest hubs, walkthrough videos and ledgers, an interactive notes workbench, a Quest Idea Forge and a digs history collection.
eras.backend: The repository gained per-character Claude skills and agents, an agent autonomy matrix and drift guard, shared runner and claude-run references replacing vendored copies, Lighthouse CI, PostHog capture, a canonical AGENTS.md and an Astro spike.
transitions: from in-repo AI tooling to shared fleet kits referenced by version
from single quests to multi-chapter epic chains with verified walkthroughs

learnings.lesson: Reference shared actions and gems rather than vendoring copies; several vendored generators and runners had to be retired.
Build retry handling into autonomous loops from the start; the quest-perfection loop needed hardening against transient failures.
Choose remote theme vs vendored theme up front; years of Sass and layout churn ended in a single 8k-line deletion.
Settle the content taxonomy and URLs once; collections were created, consolidated and deleted repeatedly, and quest permalinks eventually needed redirects.
Validate frontmatter in CI before generating content in bulk; it would have avoided the 318-error and 641-file cleanup passes.
Never commit generated artifacts such as link-check dumps and logs; they repeatedly bloated the history and were then removed.
Keep external material in its own repos from the start; vendored wargame docs, the posts collection and bookstore scripts all had to be moved out.
Standardize secrets and shared CI pieces once; token renames and vendored runner copies caused repeated workflow repairs.

transitions.to: Jekyll site on the zer0 mistakes theme
a consolidated pages/ tree under beta releases

transitions.from: a broad blog, notebooks and wargames hub

transitions.to: a shared fleet runner kit and claude-run action
